gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 12 build gate now runs the landed nvme PCI starter beside the phase12 surveys so the complex-driver lane stays reviewable in one bounded path.

The first bounded starter is now landed around a lab-only queue planner that validates queue geometry, computes DMA page demand, assigns monotonic queue identifiers, and tracks doorbell offsets without claiming live PCI behavior.
Dedicated driver tests now keep the starter honest around admin and I/O queue planning, DMA page rounding, invalid geometry rejection, and reset-time queue freeze behavior.
The slice note records what the landed queue planner covers so the survey can focus on the remaining roadmap gap instead of re-explaining the starter surface.
The existing virtio_net survey keeps the broader Phase 12 checkpoint visible, which helps compare the nvme PCI lane against the tranche's other complex-driver work.
A dedicated survey gate is the smallest truthful way to record that the first nvme PCI starter has landed while the deeper transport and DMA roadmap work remains intentionally incomplete.
The lane needs an archival note that compares the current starter against the roadmap so future runs do not mistake the queue planner for a production PCI port.

The next honest nvme PCI step is one tiny PRP or SGL-facing buffer-shape helper that describes descriptor fanout limits without crossing into live DMA mapping, request submission, or hardware-backed queue setup.

Host Memory Buffer management, blk-mq queue_rq paths, live PCI queue creation, IRQ-driven completion polling, timeout recovery plumbing, and real PRP or SGL DMA mapping remain blocked until one smaller descriptor-shape helper exists and the roadmap-approved DMA-safe transport substrate is in place.
